name: General Mills, Inc.
moat_justification: Iconic brands (Cheerios, Betty Crocker, Pillsbury, Nature Valley, Blue Buffalo) and shelf/distribution scale, with ROIC_proxy of 11-13% in FY2022-25 and gross margin held in a 32.6-34.9% band — above cost of capital but narrowing, not wide-moat grade; pricing power is now exhausted (private-label share gains, volumes falling), and the FY2026 North America Pet goodwill impairment shows the premium pet franchise was overpaid for and is weakening.
fragility_flags: BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 3.6%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 6.2x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier C (10.7%) vs bull-case tier B (16.1%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: Solid branded-food franchise, moat 5/10, in a volume/impairment downcycle — does not clear 15% at $32.81 (weighted IRR 12.9% on the normalized base, IV@15% $27.50; on the TTM base only 9.6%, Tier D); clears 15% only below $27.50.
moat_for: Iconic brand portfolio (Cheerios, Betty Crocker, Pillsbury, Nature Valley, Old El Paso, Häagen-Dazs, Blue Buffalo) with national shelf space and distribution scale
ROIC_proxy stayed 11.1-13.2% across FY2022-25 (fundamentals.json) — above cost of capital through the inflation cycle
Gross margin held in a narrow 32.6-34.9% band over the last five fiscal years despite input-cost inflation
Category positions across cereal, snacks, meals, baking and premium pet that retailers must stock
moat_against: Pricing power exhausted: 2022-23 price hikes widened the gap to private label, which is taking unit share in cereal and snacks; volumes are falling
ROIC trend is down (13.2% FY2022 to 11.1% FY2025, 3.4% reported FY2026 on impairments) and gross margin is flat, not expanding
FY2026 impairments — $1,500M North America Pet goodwill plus $250M Nudges/True Chews brands — are an admission the Blue Buffalo-era pet moat is narrower than paid for
GLP-1 drugs and value-seeking consumers shrink stomach share for cereal/snack categories
Net debt $13,084.2M is 6.2x normalized OE; buybacks are paused for deleveraging, removing the per-share tailwind
